source.product: No real product. An invented warm-Japandi round solid white-oak side table, a circular chamfered top on three slim splayed tapered legs, backing a synthetic stub listing.
source.generation: Four-view turnaround sheet (codex-image), cropped at detected gutter boundaries by scripts/turnaround_crop.mjs, then Higgsfield multi_image_to_3d (Meshy) with should_texture, enable_pbr, should_remesh, triangle topology, target_polycount 28000, symmetry_mode auto, and an oak texture_prompt.
source.postProcessing: gltf-transform resize to 1024 px textures (resize only, no lossy re-encode, geometry untouched), then scripts/fit_glb.py 45 45 55.
source.dimensionsVerifiedAt: Not a retail product; nothing external to verify against. The declared dimensions are what the mesh measures.
source.priceVerifiedAt: None. price_cents on the stub listing is invented demo data.

knownLimitations: Generic visual proxy, not a real SKU. It may only back a synthetic stub listing.

The piece is close to rotationally symmetric, so the four source views carry little independent information about the sides and rear. The leg spacing and the exact leg-to-top junction are inferred rather than observed.
The underside of the top is generated, not observed.

fit_glb.py reached 45 x 45 x 55 cm exactly (exit 0, residual 0.00 on every axis) using a per-axis scale at 7.46 percent anisotropy, so the mesh is slightly stretched relative to what the generator produced. The footprint stayed square, so the top should still read as circular.
frontAxis +Z is nominal only. With three legs the piece has no meaningful front, and rotating it about Y is harmless.
Visual quality has NOT been verified in a render. Only measurements, top-surface flatness, triangle count and byte size were checked against the file.
